title: FORCE-FED PRODUCTS
notes: Chapter 19 was enacted by Local Law 2019/202 (Intro. 1378-2019), passed by the NYC Council on October 30, 2019, and approved by the Mayor on November 25, 2019. The law took effect on November 25, 2022 (three years after signing). Enforcement was delayed by litigation; the NYC Appellate Division upheld the ban in March 2026. The law bans the sale of foie gras and any other force-fed bird products in retail food establishments and food service establishments.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.text:
For the purposes of this chapter, the following terms have the following meanings:
"Food service establishment" means a place where food is provided for individual portion service directly to the consumer whether such food is provided free of charge or sold, and whether consumption occurs on or off the premises or is provided from a pushcart, stand or vehicle.
"Force-feeding" means the practice of forcing, by any means, food or supplements into the throat, esophagus, crop or stomach of an animal.
"Force-fed product" means any product that is the result of force-feeding a bird, including but not limited to a duck or a goose, with the intent to fatten or enlarge the bird's liver.
"Retail food establishment" means any establishment that offers food for sale for off-premises consumption.

sections.title: Prohibited conduct
sections.text: No person, or any agent thereof, shall sell or offer for sale, or in any food service establishment provide or offer to provide by sale or any other manner, any force-fed product.

sections.title: Enforcement
sections.text: The department shall enforce the provisions of this chapter. Any person who violates any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished by a fine of no more than one thousand dollars, or a term of imprisonment for no more than one year, or both, for each such violation.
